newsitem.title: USA: Phone group asks FCC to quash SBC long-distance bid.
newsitem.headline: Phone group asks FCC to quash SBC long-distance bid.

text.p: A phone industry group urged regulators Wednesday to quash SBC Communications Inc.'s landmark bid to offer long-distance service, saying the Baby Bell does not face real competition on its home turf.

The Association for Local Telecommunications Services (ALTS) also called on the Federal Communications Commission to slap a penalty on SBC alleging that SBC knowingly gave the agency wrong information in its application about a competitor.

The association, which helped torpedo a similar bid by Chicago-based Ameritech Corp., argued that SBC does not face competition for residential local phone service in Oklahoma. The San Antonio, Texas-based parent of Southwestern Bell wants to offer long-distance calling to Oklahoma residents.

"SBC's long-distance 'trial balloon' should never have left the ground," said Heather Gold, president of ALTS, which represents about 33 companies offering local service in competition with the regional Bells.
She called SBC's bid "frivolous and premature."

Under the 1996 communications act, SBC and other Bells generally must show they face competition from another carrier offering business and residential phone service before winning FCC approval to enter the $80 billion long-distance business.

SBC accused ALTS of trying to delay its long-distance entry. SBC Senior Vice President Zeke Robertson said the carrier's application meets the requirements of the law "and is supported on all matters of fact."
